{"id":"mimid-1wgh.130","title":"An invite to a call room cannot be told apart from any other invite: record::Invite has no parent","design":"Found 2026-11-24 while finishing bead mimid-1wgh.114.6 (the IRC notice),
and recorded there first. Split out because fixing it is work in
mimid-agent-core, not in a front end.

WHAT IS MISSING. crates/mimid-agent-store/src/record.rs's Invite has no
parent field, because Agent::invite_details does not surface the
Welcome's parent_room (room-policy-04 §5). So a front end cannot tell an
invite to a CALL room from an invite to any other room.

WHY IT MATTERS. A call is its own parent-dependent room and
Store::start_call invites the chat's people into it (decision
mimid-1wgh.113). With the default `invites = "any"` the invite is
accepted and never shown, so nothing is wrong today. With a stricter
invite policy it becomes a pending invite to a room the user cannot
usefully enter:

  - on IRC, to a room that gets no channel even once joined
    (mimid-agent-irc::names, bead mimid-1wgh.114.6), so accepting it
    appears to do nothing;
  - on any front end, with no way to say "this is a call" in the prompt,
    so the user is asked a question they cannot answer sensibly.

The announcement of bead mimid-1wgh.114.1 does not help: it is a message
in the PARENT chat, and the invite arrives on its own path, possibly
before or without it.

WHAT TO DO, in order:

1. mimid-agent-core: carry parent_room out of the Welcome's room policy
   into Agent::invite_details. The information is already there -- the
   joining side reads the parent from the policy, which is how
   Store::start_call's room is recognised as a call after joining
   (tests/calls.rs reads Room::parent on bob's side). It is not kept on
   the INVITE.
2. mimid-agent-store: Invite gains the parent room's URI, and the record
   migration that goes with it.
3. Front ends decide what to do with it. The honest default is to accept
   a call invite the way `invites = "any"` does regardless of policy,
   since the call is already confined to the parent's people and the
   policy's purpose is to stop strangers opening rooms -- but that is a
   decision and belongs in its own bead if it is taken.

NOT URGENT: with the default policy nothing is visible. It matters the
first time someone runs a stricter one, and it will look like a bug in
calls rather than in invites.
